role: SHIPPED. The third grammar candidate to ship, and the first aimed at the extension-SCRIPT surface rather than at the plpgsql language.

target.howItWasChosen: The recall metric that had been driving this lane was corrected first (see recallMetricCorrection in v6-plpgsql-shipped.json): by distinct NAME, functions stood at 834/1170 and the count ratio had been pointing at tables. Classifying all 250 missing names by cause gave the actionable bucket: 156 were ordinary TOP-LEVEL declarations lost to cascade damage in a file the grammar could not parse, 93 were inside EXECUTE string literals (unrecoverable by design), 1 was in a body.
target.diagnosis: Only 4 of 387 extension-corpus files parsed with zero errors. Clustering the ERROR spans by first-two-tokens and ranking by FILE COUNT put psql meta-commands first: the backslash-echo usage banner every extension install script opens with appeared in 301 of 302 damaged files, ahead of every SQL construct. A minimal repro made it a LOSS rather than noise: a backslash-set followed by CREATE FUNCTION yields create_function = 0.
target.alsoFixed: LANGUAGE 'sql' (156 files) and the C-language body `AS 'modulename', 'symbolname'` (156 files), both of which left a trailing ERROR in every file that used them.

thePlacementDecision.question: A psql directive is not SQL, so where does it belong?
designsBuiltAndRejected: 1. A `program` item: a name token plus `repeat(token(/[^\n\\;]+/))` of argument tokens. Ran the generator for 127 MINUTES without emitting a parse table.
2. A single collapsed token inside `program` (`token(seq('\\\\', /[A-Za-z_]+/, /[^\n;]*/))`). Ran for 66 minutes, also without a table.
thePlacementDecision.shipped: An `extra`. The lexer skips the directive wherever it appears, so it never enters the LR automaton at all. Same measured outcome, a fraction of the table, and the more honest placement: modelling a psql directive as a statement would imply the analyzer should extract declarations from it.
thePlacementDecision.lesson: A token that can consume an arbitrary run of text is expensive inside the LR automaton no matter how few states its rule has, because it is ambiguous against `extras` and against every statement boundary at once. Two builds were spent learning that, and the abandoned attempts are recorded in grammar.js rather than deleted.

measuredOutcome.instrument: a SELF-VERIFYING probe that prints the loaded grammar's node-type count before reporting symbol totals

instrumentFlawFoundAgain.what: The engine resolves the wasm through an IN-MEMORY REGISTRY, so writing a different file to wasm/ inside a running process does not change the bytes the analyzer loads.
instrumentFlawFoundAgain.howItMisled: Two probes disagreed on the same file (4,252 vs 4,394 function symbols) and I initially concluded V8 had REGRESSED recall, then concluded from a second faulty probe that it was neutral. The truth is that V8 is better on all three axes.
instrumentFlawFoundAgain.fix: The committed probe loads the intended wasm, prints its `nodeTypeCount` as proof of what the engine actually got, and only then reports totals. One process per grammar AND a surface assertion.
instrumentFlawFoundAgain.note: This is the THIRD time this flaw produced a wrong conclusion in this lane. It is recorded in the pin's patchEvidence as well, because a future reader comparing two builds by swapping the file will hit it again.

honestLimits: 282 of 387 extension files still contain at least one ERROR, so most of the cascade bucket remains. The next dominant shapes after this patch should be re-measured rather than assumed.
@placeholder@ templating (measured at 154 files) is NOT addressed. It needs a template token in identifier and type positions, which is invasive and was deliberately deferred rather than half-done.
93 of the originally-missing distinct names remain unrecoverable in principle: they are declared inside EXECUTE string literals whose names are composed at run time.
